mechanism_inventory: access-control mismatch — receiveFromBridge is public with no caller restriction; any EOA or contract can call it, not only a registered bridge adapter
victim accounting direction — attacker supplies arbitrary postBridge swap instructions, target, paymentOperator, payload, and refund, potentially redirecting already-held contract funds
external-call failure / DoS — attacker can supply a malicious or reverting target/payload causing executor to revert, bricking in-flight bridge completions
missing invariant enforcement — no check that msg.sender is a registered bridgeAdapter
hook caller or hook-timing mismatch — receiveFromBridge is supposed to be the bridge completion callback but caller identity is not enforced
value exceeds a logical / economic bound — attacker-controlled swapInstructions can set amountIn to drain any ERC20 pre-approved or held by UTB

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: receiveFromBridge has no access control: declared `public` with no modifier, no msg.sender check, no allowlist of registered bridge adapters. Any address can call it directly, bypassing the entire bridge flow that was supposed to fund the contract. It immediately calls _swapAndExecute, with attacker control over swapperId, target, paymentOperator, payload, refund.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Unprivileged EOA. No role, no allowance, no privileged setup beyond initiating the call.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Attacker calls receiveFromBridge(postBridge, target, paymentOperator, payload, refund) directly. 2. _swapAndExecute runs with attacker params. 3. If UTB holds residual ERC20 / in-flight bridged tokens, attacker crafts instructions to consume them; attacker controls target and payload so executor.execute is called with arbitrary target/payload. 4. attacker controls refund so refunded value flows to attacker.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Protocol users whose funds are in-flight (UTB holds bridged tokens between receipt and execution); UTB contract balance of any token; any address that has approved UTB.
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker receives execution of arbitrary calldata with protocol-held tokens, or redirects refunds.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Complete absence of access control on a function designed to be called only by registered bridge adapters; direct fund-loss path on any tokens held by or approved to UTB.

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: Attacker-controlled `payload` and `target` are passed directly to executor.execute without sanitization. Since receiveFromBridge is callable by anyone, an attacker can execute arbitrary calldata on any contract using UTB as the caller context.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Unprivileged EOA; needs only a swap instruction that yields some tokenOut, then points target at any contract.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Attacker calls receiveFromBridge with trivial swap, target=victim contract, payload=malicious calldata. 2. executor.execute invoked with attacker target/payload. 3. The call executes on the victim contract with UTB as msg.sender, abusing any permission UTB has (token approvals, role-based access where UTB is trusted).
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Any protocol/contract that trusts UTB as a caller; any token holder who approved UTB.
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker achieves arbitrary execution with UTB's identity/privileges.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Distinct from simple token theft — enables impersonation of UTB in external protocols. Different actor (external contracts trusting UTB) and state space than mechanism 1.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: Drain of UTB-held native ETH or ERC20 via attacker-supplied swap instructions when UTB has residual balances
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: UTB has receive()/fallback() payable; performSwap with tokenIn==address(0) wraps from msg.value, but a crafted swapper returning tokenOut==address(0) with amountOut from UTB's own WETH could drain to attacker refund.
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Whether a registered swapper can cause UTB to drain its own pre-existing WETH/ETH balance vs only the attacker's msg.value — depends on swapper implementation (not provided).
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: UTB contract ETH/WETH; legitimate bridge users buffered funds.

rejected_mechanisms.mechanism: Fee bypass via receiveFromBridge skipping retrieveAndCollectFees modifier
rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: receiveFromBridge intentionally has no fee modifier — it is the bridge-completion endpoint; fees were collected on the source chain in bridgeAndExecute. By design.
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: No fee to bypass at completion; the primary harm is the access-control absence (mechanism 1), not fee evasion.

impact_direction.attacker_receives: Execution of arbitrary calldata with UTB's identity; redirect of swap output and refunds; potential drain of UTB-held tokens.
impact_direction.victim_loses: Any tokens held by UTB (in-flight bridge funds); contracts trusting UTB lose that trust boundary; fee invariants violated.
impact_direction.invariant_violated: Cross-chain bridge authorization invariant fully violated: receiveFromBridge MUST only be callable by a registered bridge adapter completing a legitimate bridge message; zero enforcement.
impact_direction.not_self_funded_or_dust_or_admin_or_timi: Not self-funded (UTB holds third-party funds), not dust, not admin-only (permissionless), not timing-only.

stop_condition: more_mechanisms_pending: arbitrary-execution-via-UTB-identity carried; native ETH balance drain via crafted swapper unresolved
